```{r}
#| include: false
# body of the "Across the nation" section of scoring.qmd, knitted as a child (see the
# gate there: doc_has_share()). Every number below is read from THIS book's release
# (doc_ver()) through libs/versioned.R; a figure the release has not published renders
# as a visible placeholder, never as another release's value.
sh_ver   <- doc_ver()
sh_kappa <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(doc_method("share_kappa_pct", sh_ver)))
sh_kappa_txt <- if (length(sh_kappa) == 1 && is.finite(sh_kappa))
  paste0(format(sh_kappa), " %") else "[κ not published for this version]"
sh_den   <- doc_method("share_denom", sh_ver)
sh_den_txt <- if (is.null(sh_den)) "[headline denominator not published for this version]" else sh_den
sh_cats  <- if (exists("cats")) cats$sp_cat[cats$scored] else character(0)
sh_cats_md <- if (length(sh_cats)) paste0("`", sh_cats, "`", collapse = ", ") else "[categories not published for this version]"
sh_dsum  <- doc_taxon_denom_summary(sh_ver)
sh_n     <- function(x) if (is.null(sh_dsum)) "[taxon_denom not published for this version]" else n_fmt(sh_dsum[[x]])
```

## Across the nation: the distribution share {#sec-share}

::: {.callout-important}
## Two scores, two questions

The **ecoregionally rescaled score** (@eq-ecoregion-rescale) is relative within an ecoregion: a 100
marks the most sensitive cell for that metric *within that ecoregion*, so it is comparable among the
Program Areas of one ecoregion and answers "where, within this region, is marine life most
concentrated?".

The **distribution share**, published from v10, is comparable across the whole study area. It is the
fraction of each species' range that a cell or a zone holds, weighted by extinction risk and summed, so it
answers "how much of the nation's importance for this category is here, per square kilometre,
compared with the national average?". National tables use the share; within-region maps and rankings use
the rescaled score. Never mix the two in one column or one composite.
:::

The rescaled scores above cannot be compared across ecoregions, because every ecoregion contains a 100 by
construction. For reporting across regions, a release that carries the share family computes a second
score from the same merged models, in which every species is first normalized to itself. The
within-ecoregion metrics are kept unchanged beside it, as the control.

### The species share and the category share

A species' share of a cell is the part of its whole modelled range that the cell holds, where the range is
measured as suitability times area:

$$
\text{share}_{s,c} = \frac{v_{s,c}\, A_c}{\sum_{c' \in \text{range}(s)} v_{s,c'}\, A_{c'}}
$$ {#eq-share-species}

where $v_{s,c}$ is the merged value of species $s$ in cell $c$ (@sec-model-merging) and $A_c$ is the area of
the cell. The shares of one species sum to 1 over its whole range (inside the nation they sum to the species' US fraction), and the build asserts it. The denominator runs
over the species' **whole modelled range**, land included, because the merged global surfaces keep a bird's
entire range; a cell that is not in the ocean grid takes the area of its latitude row. Where a species has no
merged global surface, the denominator comes from a second source (see [Three denominators](#sec-share-denominators)
below).

Cells then sum their species within a category, weighted by extinction risk as in @eq-cell-score:

$$
\text{share}_{c,g} = \frac{1}{100} \sum_{s \in g} w_{s,c}\, \text{share}_{s,c}
$$ {#eq-share-cell}

where $w_{s,c}$ is the governing extinction-risk score (`er_score`, @sec-extinction-risk) for most species, and
100 for sea turtles, whose merged value already carries their risk (@eq-cell-score-turtle). Because the share
divides each species by its own total, the risk *level* of such a turtle cancels: its weight is 1 whatever its
status, and only the spatial pattern of risk times suitability survives. The scored categories are
`r sh_cats_md`, and primary productivity enters the composite separately, as
its own quotient (below).

### From cells to zones

A zone adds up its cells, each weighted by the part of the cell that lies inside the zone:

$$
\text{share}_{z,g} = \sum_{c} \text{share}_{c,g}\, p_{zc}
\,, \qquad
\text{pct}_{z,g} = \frac{100\; \text{share}_{z,g}}{\sum_{s \in g} w_s / 100}
\,, \qquad
\text{pct}^{\text{nation}}_{z,g} = \frac{100\; \text{share}_{z,g}}{\text{share}_{\text{USA},g}}
$$ {#eq-share-zone}

where $p_{zc}$ is the coverage of cell $c$ by zone $z$ (`zone_cell.pct_covered` ÷ 100). Cell area enters
twice: in the numerator of the species share (@eq-share-species), and through $p_{zc}$ as the area of the cell
that is inside the zone, $A_c\,p_{zc}$. This is the v10 rule, and it differs from how the ecoregionally
rescaled scores are aggregated, which weights by coverage alone (@sec-scoring-zone-aggregation).
$\text{pct}_{z,g}$ is the **percent of the world's** risk-weighted importance for the category that lies inside
the zone, the *amount at stake*; $\text{pct}^{\text{nation}}_{z,g}$ is the **percent of the nation's**. Both are totals and
grow with the zone's area.

The score removes the area:

$$
\text{v10}_{z,g} = 100 \; \frac{\text{share}_{z,g} \,/\, \text{share}_{\text{USA},g}}{A_z \,/\, A_{\text{USA}}}
$$ {#eq-v10}

with $A_z = \sum_c A_c\, p_{zc}$, and $\text{share}_{\text{USA},g}$ and $A_{\text{USA}}$ the same sums over the
national reference. The reference is the **study area**: every cell flagged `in_usa`, each in full. It is not
the `USA` pseudo-zone, which is the union of the subregion polygons and omits coastal and estuarine
study-area cells that carry scored species.

The score is the zone's fraction of the nation's importance for the category divided by its fraction of the
nation's surface. It is a location quotient [@isserman1977]: 100 means the zone holds exactly its fair
share of the component per square kilometre, 300 three times the national concentration, 20 a fifth of it.
The reference point is therefore fixed and identical for every zone and every component, it does not depend on
any other zone's score, and it is stable across releases. In the reference-point typology of the Ocean Health
Index it is a distance to a reference rather than a comparison with the best performer
[@halpern2012; @samhouri2012; @oecd2008].

Because the zone total sums over species, it equals the number of species present times their mean
risk-weighted fraction: richness still counts, once per species rather than once per cell, and both factors
are published beside the score (`_n_species`, `_mean_share_*`) so that a reader can tell an area that scores by
richness from one that scores by dependence. No richness-damping exponent is applied.

In the language of conservation planning the zone total is rarity-weighted richness [@williams1996;
@albuquerque2015] and weighted endemism [@crisp2001] computed on a suitability surface with a risk weight, and
it is the per-feature normalization Zonation applies to every input layer [@moilanen2005]. It rewards
irreplaceability [@kukkala2013]: a zone holding an entire endemic population scores at the top, a zone holding
a few vagrants near zero, and no species-rich region can dominate merely by count. It is blind to the dense
habitat of wide-ranging species, which is what the ecoregional score continues to show. Its denominator is a
modelling choice whose reference area is stated, as the national-responsibility literature requires
[@schmeller2008; @schmeller2014], and it follows the global-population thresholds of site designation
[@iucn2016kba; @ramsar2005].

### Primary productivity and the composite

Primary productivity has no species. Its quotient is the zone's mean productivity over the national mean, on
the same scale:

$$
\text{v10}_{z,\text{primprod}} = 100 \; \frac{\bar{n}_z}{\bar{n}_{\text{USA}}}
$$ {#eq-share-primprod}

where $\bar{n}_z$ is the area-weighted mean of net primary productivity over all of the zone's cells (a cell
without a value counts as 0, as the published `pct_area` down-weighting does for the rescaled score) and
$\bar{n}_{\text{USA}}$ is the same estimator over the national reference.

The composite is the equal-weight mean of the components that are reportable in the zone, each on the same
scale, so it too reads 100 for a zone that is nationally average across the board. A component that is not
reportable (next subsection) is left out of the mean, exactly as a category with no cells in the zone is.
Equal weights are a stated policy choice, the convention of the Ocean Health Index [@halpern2012]. The
re-issued Program-Area table in the release chapter reports, per category, the score, the percent of the
world's importance at stake and the rank change against the ecoregional ranking, with the Spearman rank
correlation between the two composite rankings in its caption [@oecd2008].

### The reporting floor {#sec-share-floor}

A component is reported for a zone only if its scored cells cover at least $\kappa$ of the zone's area,
where coverage is the area-weighted fraction of the zone's cells that carry a value for the category:

$$
\text{cov}_{z,g} = \frac{\sum_{c \in z:\ \text{share}_{c,g}\ \text{exists}} p_{zc} A_c}{\sum_{c \in z} p_{zc} A_c}
\;\ge\; \kappa
$$ {#eq-share-floor}

with $\kappa$ = `r sh_kappa_txt` in `r sh_ver`. Below the floor the component is not reportable: it is shown
as no data on maps, footnoted in tables, and left out of the composite. It is never set to zero, which would
lower the composite for a reason unrelated to sensitivity. The floor is defined on the footprint, not on the
value. It applies to the across-the-nation family only: the within-ecoregion rows of the same release are the
control and carry no floor.

```{r}
#| label: share-floor-count
#| results: asis
cv <- doc_zone_metric(sh_ver, like = "%!_coverage")
if (!is.null(cv) && nrow(cv) && is.finite(sh_kappa)) {
  below <- cv[cv$val < sh_kappa / 100, ]
  cat(sprintf(
    "In %s the floor removes **%s** Program Area × component pair%s of the %s that have scored cells.\n\n",
    sh_ver, n_fmt(nrow(below)), if (nrow(below) == 1) "" else "s", n_fmt(nrow(cv))))
} else cat("*The number of Program Area × component pairs the floor removes is read from the release's `_coverage` metrics, which this release has not published.*\n\n")
```

### Three denominators, one flag {#sec-share-denominators}

The headline divides each species by its whole modelled range (`global`). Two other denominators are
computed beside it, as columns of the same table, so that a reader can see how much the choice matters:

| Denominator | Divides the species by | In words |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `global` (headline) | its value-area over its whole modelled range | the species' fraction of the world that a cell holds |
| `usa` | its value-area over its US cells | the same score with the species weight $w$ in place of $w\,f_{\text{US}}$, where $f_{\text{US}}$ is the species' US fraction of its range; every species sums to 1 inside the nation |
| `pooled` | 1 (no per-species normalization) | value times area summed over species; the national reference divides it out |

: The three denominators. The headline is a release setting (`share_denom` in the release's `release_method` rows: `r sh_den_txt`); the other two are always written beside it. {#tbl-share-denominators}

Where a species has no merged global surface, its denominator is built from the best source available, in
this order: a curated fallback fraction of the world's range that lies in US waters (for species whose
only models are national, such as FWS and NMFS range maps); the merged global surface; and, for species
modelled only by AquaMaps, the AquaMaps footprint outside the US plus the merged surface inside. The source
of every species is recorded in the `taxon_denom` table.

```{r}
#| label: share-denom-counts
#| results: asis
if (is.null(sh_dsum)) {
  cat("*The count of species per denominator source is read from the release's `taxon_denom` table, which this release has not published.*\n\n")
} else cat(sprintf(
  "In %s, of %s scored species, %s take the merged global surface, %s the AquaMaps footprint outside the US plus the merged surface inside, and %s a curated fallback fraction; %s are unresolved.\n\n",
  sh_ver, n_fmt(sh_dsum$n), n_fmt(sh_dsum$merged_global), n_fmt(sh_dsum$aquamaps),
  n_fmt(sh_dsum$fallback), n_fmt(sh_dsum$unresolved + sh_dsum$other)))
```

A separate **sensitivity column** treats the floored cells of the sea turtles. A turtle's merged value is
floored at 1 where its suitability rounds to 0, which fills the range rather than describing habitat. The
headline keeps those cells, so the surface stays continuous; the `_strip` column removes them from both sides of the share.

### What is published

| Key | Level | Meaning |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `extrisk_{g}_share_{d}` | cell, zone | risk-weighted share summed over category $g$ (@eq-share-cell); the zone key is the zone total (@eq-share-zone) |
| `extrisk_{g}_v10_{d}` | cell, zone | the score (@eq-v10); absent in a zone where the component is not reportable |
| `extrisk_{g}_pct_world`, `extrisk_{g}_pct_nation_{d}` | zone | percent of the world's, and of the nation's, importance in the zone |
| `extrisk_{g}_coverage`, `_n_species`, `_mean_share_{d}` | zone | the floor's coverage, the number of species present, and the zone total divided by it |
| `primprod_v10`, `primprod_coverage` | zone | the productivity quotient (@eq-share-primprod) and its coverage |
| `score_v10_equalweights_{d}`, `score_v10_n_components_{d}` | cell, zone | the composite and the number of components it averages (per cell: every component present, no floor) |

: Metric keys of the share family. $d$ is `global`, `usa` or `pooled`; `global_strip` is the sensitivity column. Cell rasters are written for the headline denominator unless the release says otherwise. The per-species shares that explain a zone's score are in `zone_taxon` (`share_global`, `share_usa`, `share_v10_contrib`). {#tbl-share-keys}

```{r}
#| label: share-verified
#| results: asis
# computed, not typed: where the nation's sea-turtle importance lies, by region
tt <- doc_zone_metric(sh_ver, keys = "extrisk_turtle_pct_nation_global")
pr <- tryCatch(sf::st_drop_geometry(sf::st_read(
  here::here("data/ply_programareas_2026_v4.gpkg"), quiet = TRUE))[, c("programarea_key", "region_name")],
  error = function(e) NULL)
if (!is.null(tt) && nrow(tt) && !is.null(pr)) {
  tt$region <- pr$region_name[match(tt$zone_key, pr$programarea_key)]
  by <- tapply(tt$val, tt$region, sum, na.rm = TRUE)
  cat("**Check on ", sh_ver, ".** Under the global denominator, the share of the nation's risk-weighted sea-turtle importance that lies in each region's Program Areas is ",
      paste(sprintf("%s %.1f %%", names(by), by), collapse = ", "), ".\n\n", sep = "")
}
```
